message.content:
You are a read-only scout for the live-spec night run. You MUST NOT edit, create, move, or commit anything, and must not run state-changing git commands. Read and grep only. Your final text is the deliverable.

Read the package at /private/tmp/live-spec-night18/wt-int (branch night/2026-08-18-integration) — read only, do not modify. Also read /private/tmp/live-spec-control/checks-census-2026-08-18.md in full.

CONTEXT. A later worker will move the guardrail checks that have never caught a real defect into guardrails/attic/, each with one line of reason. The census says: 56 checks total, 9 alive (documented live catch), 2 insufficient data, 45 never caught anything. The nine alive must not be touched. The move must be reversible and must not weaken anything that still holds.

Deliver:

1. VERIFY THE CENSUS AGAINST DISK. List every guardrails/check-*.py and check-*.sh actually present and count them. Does the total match 56? Name any check present on disk but missing from the census, and any census row naming a check that no longer exists. This matters: the census was written against an older tree, and lane D and lane A have landed since.

2. THE WIRING MAP — the important part. For EACH of the 45 candidates, report where it is wired:
   - is it invoked from guardrails/pre-push? (quote the gate letter and line)
   - is it invoked from .github/workflows/gates.yml? (line)
   - is it named in scripts/check-registry.json or guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json or guardrails/named-checks or any similar roster? (file:line)
   - which tests read or execute it? (file:line for each)
   Group the 45 into: (a) wired into the push gate AND CI, (b) wired in only one place, (c) not wired anywhere — a check nobody runs.
   Group (c) is the cheapest and safest to move; group (a) is the most expensive, because moving it means editing the push gate and CI in the same package.

3. THE HIDDEN COST. Several rosters assert that every declared check exists and is reachable — guardrails/check-named-checks.py and guardrails/check-every-gate-can-fail.py are the ones to read first. Determine exactly what breaks when a check file moves to guardrails/attic/: which roster entries must move with it, which red-proof fixtures must move, and which tests assert the roster and the tree agree. Name the file:line of every such coupling. If moving any given check would require touching a protected file (.live-spec/PROBLEMS.md, .live-spec/culling-plan-v3-2026-08-10.md, docs/PROGRESS.md), say so — that check must then be left alone.

4. A RECOMMENDED ORDER for the writer: which checks to move first (cheap, unwired), which to move in a second batch, and which you would NOT move tonight and why. Be conservative: name every check whose move looks riskier than its benefit, especially any of the two "insufficient data" ones.

5. THE ONE-LINE REASONS. For each check you recommend moving, draft its one-line reason in plain words, stating what it was built to catch and that no documented live catch exists. These lines are the record the owner will read in the morning — they must be honest, not boilerplate.

Be exact with file:line. Do not recommend anything you have not verified in the tree.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

46	
47	## Практический вывод для продуктизации
48	
49	- **9 живых гейтов** — это ядро, доказавшее свою цену; держать без изменений.
50	- **45 «никогда не ловил»** не значит «удалить все» — часть из них (`check-every-gate-can-fail.py`, `check-hooks-can-fire.py`) — намеренно мета/self-test гейты, их роль не «ловить дефект продукта», а держать остальные гейты честными; часть (`check-listener-tripwire.py`) ждёт условия, которое ещё не наступило. Но заметная доля (`check-doc-bound.py`, `check-earned-message.py`, `check-board.py`, `check-freeze.sh`, `check-judge-listed.py`, `check-index-generated.py`, `check-config-surface.py`, `check-doc-findings-bound.py` — самый дорогой чек без единой поимки) — кандидаты на honest-proof ревизию: либо усилить/сделать реалистичный red-fixture и подтвердить, что они вообще могут поймать что-то на реальном дереве, либо явно пометить как cost-без-пользы.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
3	# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
4	# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
5	#
6	# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
7	# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
8	# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
13	cd "$REPO_ROOT"
14	GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"
15	
16	# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
17	# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
18	# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
19	# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
20	# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
21	# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
22	# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
23	# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
24	# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
25	#
26	# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
27	# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
28	# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
29	# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
30	# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
31	if [ -t 0 ]; then
32	  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
33	else
34	  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
35	fi
36	export PUSH_REF_LINES
37	if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
38	  set +e
39	  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
40	  del_code=$?
41	  set -e
42	  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
43	    echo "$del_out"
44	    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
45	    exit 0
46	  fi
47	fi
48	
49	fail=0
50	
51	echo "== live-spec push gate =="
52	
53	echo ""
54	echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
55	set +e
56	reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
57	reach_code=$?
58	set -e
59	echo "$reach_out"
60	
61	echo ""
62	echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
63	# The reach verdict does not scope this gate (the 2718c69 stand-down, reverted on the owner's
64	# 2026-08-15 word). A prose-only or scoped diff still sends commits, and the record this gate
65	# demands is the adversarial read of the pushed RANGE (INV-304) — a thing no file-class verdict
66	# can stand down for. The only stand-downs that exist are the two PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226.6 names
67	# by hand: a deletion-only push (handled above, before this chain) and the recordless class.
68	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
69	  fail=1
70	fi
71	
72	echo ""
73	echo "-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --"
74	case "$reach_code" in
75	  0)
76	    echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
77	    ;;
78	  2)
79	    scoped_files="$(printf '%s\n' "$reach_out" | sed -n 's/^SCOPED //p')"
80	    if ! SCOPED_TEST_FILES="$scoped_files" "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
81	      fail=1
82	    fi
83	    ;;
84	  *)
85	    if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
86	      fail=1
87	    fi
88	    ;;
89	esac
90	
91	echo ""
92	echo "-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --"
93	echo "   Covered by gate b: tests/test_traceability.py already asserts this"
94	echo "   (test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once) — no separate check needed here."
95	
96	echo ""
97	echo "-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --"
98	if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-matrix-reference.py" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.md"; then

103	echo "-- gate g: pin drift --"

105	  fail=1
106	fi

111	fi

115	  fail=1
116	fi

120	  fail=1

131	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-muted-launch.sh"; then
132	  fail=1

137	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-cleanup-notice.sh"; then
138	  fail=1
139	fi

142	echo "-- gate p: touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205) --"
143	if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-touchpoint-kind.py"; then
144	  fail=1
145	fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
#
# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$del_out"
    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

fail=0

echo "== live-spec push gate =="

echo ""
echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
set +e
reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
reach_code=$?
set -e
echo "$reach_out"

echo ""
echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
# The reach verdict does not scope this gate (the 2718c69 stand-down, reverted on the owner's
# 2026-08-15 word). A prose-only or scoped diff still sends commits, and the record this gate
# demands is the adversarial read of the pushed RANGE (INV-304) — a thing no file-class verdict
# can stand down for. The only stand-downs that exist are the two PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226.6 names
# by hand: a deletion-only push (handled above, before this chain) and the recordless class.
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --"
case "$reach_code" in
  0)
    echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
    ;;
  2)
    scoped_files="$(printf '%s\n' "$reach_out" | sed -n 's/^SCOPED //p')"
    if ! SCOPED_TEST_FILES="$scoped_files" "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
      fail=1
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
      fail=1
    fi
    ;;
esac

echo ""
echo "-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --"
echo "   Covered by gate b: tests/test_traceability.py already asserts this"
echo "   (test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once) — no separate check needed here."

echo ""
echo "-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-matrix-reference.py" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate g: pin drift --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-pin-drift.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate f: skill loadability --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-loadability.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate e: prototype fence --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prototype-fence.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-shipped-language.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate j: no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-broad-kill.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate l: muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-muted-launch.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate o: cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-cleanup-notice.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate p: touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-touchpoint-kind.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate q: waiting list (the board loses nothing — no over-cap shown set, no demotion into the void, SPEC INV-206) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-board.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate r: authority anchor (a decision recorded as the person's names its exchange, SPEC INV-207) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-authority-anchor.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate s: skill review (a substantive skill change carries its skill-creator review record, SPEC INV-208) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-review.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate t: doc rotation (the pack's split-and-rotated docs lose nothing — every rotated row is findable in its archive and every archive is named in a manifest line, SPEC INV-209) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-rotation.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate m: config health (installed hooks match guardrails/ source, SPEC INV-175) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-config-health.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate k: compaction freeze (guarded docs' anchor map / markers / numbers unchanged, 2.0) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-freeze.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate n: the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189) --"
# Report-only at push (the owner's word, 2026-08-07 11:19): a deposit is recorded on arrival and
# never blocks a push. The check's judging moment is the intake sweep, which declines an unearned
# deposit at the door. Here it prints what the sweep will meet and the push proceeds either way.
if [ -f "$GUARDRAILS/check-earned-message.py" ] && [ -d "$REPO_ROOT/inbox" ]; then
  python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-earned-message.py" "$REPO_ROOT/inbox" || \
    echo "   (deposits above await the intake sweep; a deposit never blocks a push)"
else
  echo "   (no inbox in this tree — the gate stands down by name)"
fi

# The named-reference presence nets (SPEC INV-239) take NO push-gate letter and are NOT invoked here:
# they RIDE THE SUITE (gate b), the same placement the far-tier report-shape check takes. Their suite
# tests run each net against the real tree and assert the expected result, so a real violation reds
# the suite and gate b already blocks this push. A suite-riding check carries no gate letter, so the
# letter-counting meta-guards (INV-210, INV-212) need not see it and no gate-red-proofs / ci-mirror
# entry is owed.

echo ""
echo "-- gate h: the four host checks (this repo attached as its own first host, SPEC INV-97) --"
for hostcheck in completeness tests_present traces_to_spec conflicts; do
  if ! python3 "$REPO_ROOT/scaffold/guardrails/check_${hostcheck}.py" --base origin/main; then
    fail=1
  fi
done

echo ""
echo "-- gate u: CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-ci-mirror.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate v: judges listed (every wired chat judge is referenced in the installed settings.json, SPEC INV-211) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-judge-listed.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate w: every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-every-gate-can-fail.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate x: generated index (the committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-index-generated.py" "$REPO_ROOT/PRODUCT_SPEC.md" "$REPO_ROOT/PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate y: agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-agent-card.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate z: doc bound (each growable working doc within its declared bound or freshly rotated, SPEC INV-234) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-bound.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate aa: doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count; a cleared document stays at zero, SPEC INV-301) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-findings-bound.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate ad: published tree counts (every count this repository publishes about its own tree matches the tree, and the reproduction command beside it returns the published number, SPEC INV-305) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-tree-counts.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate ae: named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-named-checks.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "PUSH BLOCKED — one or more gates above failed. Fix them and try again."
  exit 1
fi

# The gates are green, so this push is about to land — sync the standalone mirror repos
# from the pack now, so a mirror never drifts behind a shipped pack version again (a mirror
# was found one version behind on 2026-07-13). This runs ONLY past the blocked-push exit
# above, so a blocked push never reaches a mirror. It is NON-BLOCKING: a mirror hiccup
# (gh not authenticated, no network) warns and lets the pack push through — the CI arm and
# the next push both re-sync. Extends the push gate (SPEC M-6) and the mirror mechanism
# (scripts/sync-mirrors.sh, SPEC INV-96).
echo ""
echo "-- mirror sync (non-blocking) --"
if "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/sync-mirrors.sh"; then
  :
else
  echo "   warn: mirror sync did not complete (gh auth? network?) — run scripts/sync-mirrors.sh by hand."
fi

echo "All gates green — push allowed."
exit 0

# gates.yml — the CI mirror of the push gate (SPEC M-5, ROADMAP row 14).
# Same checks, one source of truth: CI runs the SAME scripts the local pre-push hook
# runs — it never redefines them. This is the SECOND net: the local reach map
# (SPEC INV-45) is a developer-latency optimization; the CI net always runs the full set.
name: gates
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  gates:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      TZ: Asia/Jerusalem   # gate (a) wants a today-dated prover record; "today" is the author's day, not UTC's
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0    # gate (a)'s freshness rule reads commit history (record vs PRODUCT_SPEC.md)
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: install pytest
        run: pip install pytest
      # The external canon, pinned. Before this step existed the suite ran with no clone,
      # so every assertion that reads the externalized product-prover skipped on every CI
      # run forever, and CI claimed a green it had not earned (ROADMAP row 622 territory;
      # the same fork the emergency branch reached from the other side). The pack now
      # INSTALLS the canon rather than pretending to prove it: --ref names the exact commit
      # the pack's assertions are written against, and --expect-commit verifies the checkout
      # landed there, so a moved tag or branch cannot change what CI proves. Moving the pin
      # is a deliberate pack change; tests/test_prover_adapter_contract.py holds its shape.
      - name: install the external product-prover canon (pinned, gate b's evidence)
        run: >-
          scripts/install-external-skills.sh
          --ref 94d36454d55438951311d302fc86adba33123868
          --expect-commit 94d36454d55438951311d302fc86adba33123868
      - name: test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)
        run: python3 -m pytest -q
      - name: gate a — fresh prover record (one record per push, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304)
        # LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE lets the script judge the inbox-only carve-out (row 269,
        # SPEC M-6/INV-112): a push whose diff is exactly one new inbox/ file owes no
        # fresh record. The same base carries the range arm, which reads the pushed delta
        # against the state the remote already holds. github.event.before is the pre-push
        # SHA on a push; on a PR it is empty and the script falls back to origin/main,
        # which the fetch-depth-0 checkout above carries.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: guardrails/check-prover-record.sh --push
      - name: gate d — matrix Reference generated and agrees with the body
        run: python3 guardrails/check-matrix-reference.py TEST_MATRIX.md
      - name: gate g — pin drift
        run: guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh
      - name: gate f — skill loadability
        run: guardrails/check-skill-loadability.sh
      - name: gate e — prototype fence
        run: guardrails/check-prototype-fence.sh
      - name: gate i — shipped language (no owner name / stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120)
        run: guardrails/check-shipped-language.sh
      - name: gate j — no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162)
        run: guardrails/check-broad-kill.sh
      - name: gate l — muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157)
        run: guardrails/check-muted-launch.sh
      - name: gate o — cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204)
        run: guardrails/check-cleanup-notice.sh
      - name: gate p — touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-touchpoint-kind.py
      - name: gate q — waiting list (the board loses nothing — no over-cap shown set, no demotion into the void, SPEC INV-206)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-board.py
      - name: gate r — authority anchor (a decision recorded as the person's names its exchange, SPEC INV-207)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-authority-anchor.py
      - name: gate s — skill review (a substantive skill change carries its skill-creator review record, SPEC INV-208)
        # LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE lets the gate read the push range (the same base as gate a); on a PR it
        # is empty and the gate falls back to origin/main.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: guardrails/check-skill-review.sh
      - name: gate t — doc rotation (the pack's split-and-rotated docs lose nothing, SPEC INV-209)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-doc-rotation.py
      - name: gate h — the four host checks (this repo attached as its own first host, SPEC INV-97)
        # The base ladder mirrors gate a: github.event.before on a push, else a fetched origin/main,
        # else HEAD~1 — so the host checks compare against a ref that exists on any CI checkout.
        run: |
          base="${{ github.event.before }}"
          if [ -z "$base" ] || ! git cat-file -e "${base}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            git fetch -q origin main 2>/dev/null || true
            base="origin/main"
          fi
          if ! git cat-file -e "${base}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then base="HEAD~1"; fi
          for c in completeness tests_present traces_to_spec conflicts; do
            python3 scaffold/guardrails/check_${c}.py --base "$base"
          done
      - name: gate n — the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189)
        run: |
          # Report-only (the owner's word, 2026-08-07 11:19): a deposit never blocks a push;
          # the intake sweep is the judging moment.
          if [ -d inbox ]; then
            python3 guardrails/check-earned-message.py inbox || \
              echo "deposits above await the intake sweep; a deposit never blocks a push"
          else
            echo "no inbox in this checkout — the gate stands down by name"
          fi
      # The named-reference presence nets (SPEC INV-239) take NO push-gate letter: they RIDE THE SUITE
      # (the pytest step, gate b), the same placement the far-tier report-shape check takes, so they
      # need no separate CI step here and no ci-mirror carve-out — a suite-riding check carries no gate
      # letter for the mirror to track.
      - name: gate u — CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210)
        run: guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh
      - name: gate w — every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-every-gate-can-fail.py
      - name: gate x — generated index (committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-index-generated.py PRODUCT_SPEC.md PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md
      - name: gate y — agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-agent-card.py
      - name: gate z — doc bound (each growable working doc within its declared bound or freshly rotated, SPEC INV-234)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-doc-bound.py
      - name: gate aa — doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count, SPEC INV-301)
        # The record arm reads the record against the state the remote already holds (SPEC R302.12).
        # github.event.before is the pre-push SHA on a push; on a PR it is empty and the arm falls back
        # to origin/main, which the fetch-depth-0 checkout above carries.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py
      - name: gate ad — published tree counts (a count this repository publishes about its own tree is built from the tree, SPEC INV-305)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-tree-counts.py
      - name: gate ae — named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306)
        run: python3 guardrails/check-named-checks.py

  # After the gates pass on a real push to main, sync the standalone mirror repos from the
  # pack — the durable, cross-machine arm of the same job the local pre-push hook does (the
  # local hook covers this machine; CI covers any machine, including a browser/cloud session).
  # Auth is a per-mirror SSH deploy key held in the MIRROR_SYNC_DEPLOY_KEY secret. The job
  # skips cleanly when that secret is absent, so CI never reds for a missing key (honest
  # failure by name, SPEC INV-112). Extends the push gate (SPEC M-6) and scripts/sync-mirrors.sh
  # (SPEC INV-96).
  sync-mirrors:
    needs: gates
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false   # the mirror push authenticates with the deploy key below, not the default token
      - name: sync standalone mirrors from the pack
        env:
          MIRROR_SYNC_DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.MIRROR_SYNC_DEPLOY_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${MIRROR_SYNC_DEPLOY_KEY}" ]; then
            echo "MIRROR_SYNC_DEPLOY_KEY not set — skipping mirror sync (add the secret to enable the CI arm)."
            exit 0
          fi
          key_file="$(mktemp)"
          printf '%s\n' "${MIRROR_SYNC_DEPLOY_KEY}" > "$key_file"
          chmod 600 "$key_file"
          export GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -i $key_file -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o IdentitiesOnly=yes"
          export MIRROR_SSH=1   # tell sync-mirrors.sh to reach the mirror over SSH, not gh/HTTPS
          git config --global user.name "live-spec mirror bot"
          git config --global user.email "mirror-bot@users.noreply.github.com"
          bash scripts/sync-mirrors.sh

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# pre-commit — the concurrent-edit fence (SPEC INV-11).
     3	#
     4	# OPT-IN by design: a session arms the fence by running guardrails/fence-refresh.sh,
     5	# which writes the HEAD sha it last saw into .live-spec-fence (untracked, repo root),
     6	# plus its own session token on line 2 (ROADMAP row 572 — see guardrails/post-commit).
     7	#
     8	# If .live-spec-fence is ABSENT, this hook passes silently — the fence is not armed,
     9	# and that is deliberate, not a bug to "fix". If present and HEAD has moved since it
    10	# was recorded, another writer touched the repo; the commit is blocked until the
    11	# fence is reviewed and refreshed.
    12	#
    13	# This check only ever compares the recorded sha (line 1) to HEAD — it has no notion
    14	# of sessions itself. The session's own commits stop needing a manual refresh between
    15	# them because guardrails/post-commit re-arms the fence right after a commit that was
    16	# made by the session that currently owns the arm (row 572); a commit from a session
    17	# that doesn't own the arm still leaves the fence stale, so this check still blocks
    18	# the next commit, from anyone, exactly as before.
    19	
    20	set -euo pipefail
    21	
    22	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    23	FENCE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/.live-spec-fence"
    24	
    25	# INV-24 second arm (row 104): no staged line stamps today with a future time.
    26	if [ -x "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-future-times.sh" ]; then
    27	  "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-future-times.sh" || exit 1
    28	fi
    29	
    30	# INV-152 net: a parked-for-the-human item in the resume file or a decision page must
    31	# name its human-only fact (taste / policy / irreversible / device-feel), else it is
    32	# the seat's to do. Scans NEXT_STEPS.md and any docs/decisions/*.md.
    33	if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py" ]; then
    34	  deferral_targets=""
    35	  [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/NEXT_STEPS.md" ] && deferral_targets="$REPO_ROOT/NEXT_STEPS.md"
    36	  for d in "$REPO_ROOT"/docs/decisions/*.md; do
    37	    [ -f "$d" ] && deferral_targets="$deferral_targets $d"
    38	  done
    39	  if [ -n "$deferral_targets" ]; then
    40	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    41	    python3 "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py" $deferral_targets || exit 1
    42	  fi
    43	fi
    44	
    45	# INV-175 second arm: on a shared index, a file both staged and carrying unstaged
    46	# modifications at commit time is the signature of a second writer (or a forgotten
    47	# re-add) touching a file mid-landing. Stop, look, re-add or investigate.
    48	overlap="$(comm -12 <(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --name-only | sort -u) \
    49	                    <(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --cached --name-only | sort -u))"
    50	if [ -n "$overlap" ]; then
    51	  echo "COMMIT BLOCKED — staged files carry unstaged modifications (a second writer, or a forgotten re-add):"
    52	  echo "$overlap" | sed 's/^/  /'
    53	  echo "  Review each file (git diff <file>), then either git add it or drop the stray edit."
    54	  exit 1
    55	fi
    56	
    57	if [ ! -f "$FENCE_FILE" ]; then
    58	  exit 0
    59	fi
    60	
    61	recorded_sha="$(sed -n '1p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    62	current_sha="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)"
    63	
    64	if [ "$recorded_sha" != "$current_sha" ]; then
    65	  echo "COMMIT BLOCKED — the concurrent-edit fence is armed and HEAD has moved."
    66	  echo "  Recorded HEAD: $recorded_sha"
    67	  echo "  Current HEAD:  $current_sha"
    68	  recorded_token="$(sed -n '2p' "$FENCE_FILE" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    69	  session_token="${LIVE_SPEC_SESSION_ID:-${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}}"
    70	  if [ -n "$recorded_token" ] && [ "$recorded_token" != "$session_token" ]; then
    71	    # Restart-staleness diagnosis: after a session restart (new token) or a foreign
    72	    # window's commit, the fence blocks with no hint of WHOSE arm it is. Name it.
    73	    echo "  This arm belongs to another session (or one that has since ended) —"
    74	    echo "  not this one. It is not necessarily something to review; it may just be stale."
    75	  else
    76	    echo "  Someone else committed or pulled into this repo since your session started."
    77	  fi
    78	  echo "  Review what changed (e.g. git log $recorded_sha..$current_sha) if needed, then"
    79	  echo "  re-arm the fence for this session with the one command:"
    80	  echo "    bash guardrails/fence-refresh.sh"
    81	  exit 1
    82	fi
    83	
    84	# Plan-delta guard — his word of 2026-08-10 (DECISIONS.md), the one granted exception to the
    85	# cutting campaign's rule 2. A commit that changes the campaign plan file must stage a delta
    86	# page rooting every changed hunk. The guard stands down in a tree that has no guard script
    87	# (scratch repos, other hosts), and stands down inside the script when the plan is not staged.
    88	plan_guard="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.live-spec/check-plan-delta.sh"
    89	if [ -f "$plan_guard" ]; then
    90	  bash "$plan_guard" || exit 1
    91	fi
    92	
    93	exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check-every-gate-can-fail.py — every push gate carries a known-red proof (SPEC INV-212, gate w).

THE LAW behind it: a gate that cannot red is a check that looks at nothing — it reports green
because it never fires. This movement paid for the lesson: the authority-anchor gate shipped hollow
(commit 8a0209f rebuilt it), reporting green without reaching the surfaces it claimed to inspect,
and a worker's false "zero violations" was the same disease, a claim that protected nothing because
nothing could make it fail. So every gate the push chain runs must carry a KNOWN-RED PROOF: a
committed red-first test that drives that gate's own check to a non-zero exit, so the gate is shown
to fire. A gate with no such proof is itself the finding.

This check enumerates the gate letters guardrails/pre-push invokes — its "-- gate X:" markers, the
same enumeration check-ci-mirror.sh (gate u) reads — and requires each classified in
guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json as one of:

  * a "proof" — a red-first test `<file>::<function>` that drives the gate's check to red, tied to
    that gate by a `reds` token (usually the check's basename) the proof file must reference; or
  * "covered" — a gate that invokes no independent check of its own but rides another gate's red
    (gate c rides the pytest suite, gate b), declared with the reason it carries no separate fixture.

A registered proof is verified by reading its structure, since the suite already runs it under gate b
(exactly as check-ci-mirror.sh's own red-proof runs there): the proof file exists, the named function
is defined in it, the `reds` token appears in the file (tying the proof to this gate's check), and the
function body carries a non-zero-exit assertion, so a bare "the gate ships" presence test cannot pass
as a red proof.

A gate marker classified in none of the three maps reds — the self-widening teeth, so a gate added
later without a proof cannot slip through. A "covered" entry with no reason reds — papering over a
hollow gate is the one thing this gate exists to stop. And a gate that genuinely can never be made to
red by construction is a finding, not a carve-out: the "cannot_red" map exists so such a gate is named
loudly and reds this check, never silently waved through. A registry key naming a letter that is no
local gate is itself drift and reds, like a stale CI carve-out (INV-210).

This is the guard over the guards — a structural scan kin of config-health (INV-175) and the CI-mirror
gate (INV-210).
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(SCRIPT_DIR)

PREPUSH = os.environ.get("GATE_PROOFS_PREPUSH", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "guardrails", "pre-push"))
REGISTRY = os.environ.get("GATE_PROOFS_JSON", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "guardrails", "gate-red-proofs.json"))

GATE_MARKER = re.compile(r"-- gate ([a-z]{1,2}):")   # the chain outgrew one letter per gate

# A genuine non-zero-exit assertion, in the idioms the suite's red-proof tests use. It matches an
# assertion that the check FAILED (returncode 1/2, or not 0), or a call to a red-asserting helper.
# It deliberately does NOT match a green assertion (returncode 0) or a mere function name, so a bare
# presence test cannot pass as a red proof.
RED_ASSERT = re.compile(
    r"assert_red\(|expect_red\("
    r"|assertNotEqual\([^)\n]*(?:returncode|\bcode)\b[^)\n]*,\s*0\b"
    r"|assertEqual\([^)\n]*(?:returncode|\bcode)\b[^)\n]*,\s*[12]\b"
    r"|(?:returncode|\bcode)\s*!=\s*0\b"
    r"|(?:returncode|\bcode)\s*==\s*[12]\b"
)


def read(path):
    with open(path) as f:
        return f.read()


def gate_letters(prepush_text):
    return sorted(set(GATE_MARKER.findall(prepush_text)))


def function_body(src_text, fn):
    """The text of function `fn`: from its `def` line to the next def/class at the same or lower
    indent. Returns None if the function is not defined."""
    lines = src_text.splitlines()
    pat = re.compile(r"\bdef " + re.escape(fn) + r"\b")
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if pat.search(line):
            indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
            body = [line]
            for m in lines[i + 1:]:
                if m.strip() and (len(m) - len(m.lstrip())) <= indent and re.match(r"\s*(def |class )", m):
                    break
                body.append(m)
            return "\n".join(body)
    return None


def main():
    for f in (PREPUSH, REGISTRY):
        if not os.path.isfile(f):
            print("every-gate-can-fail: cannot read %s — the gate stands on both files." % f)
            return 1

    letters = gate_letters(read(PREPUSH))
    if not letters:
        print("every-gate-can-fail: no `-- gate X:` markers found in %s — the enumeration is empty, "
              "so the chain cannot be proven." % PREPUSH)
        return 1

    reg = json.loads(read(REGISTRY))
    proofs = reg.get("proofs", {})
    covered = reg.get("covered", {})
    cannot = reg.get("cannot_red", {})

    fail = 0

    # A registry key must name a real local gate — a stale key is drift, exactly like a stale CI
    # carve-out (INV-210).
    for section_name, section in (("proofs", proofs), ("covered", covered), ("cannot_red", cannot)):
        for k in section:
            if k not in letters:
                print("every-gate-can-fail: registry key '%s' in %s names no local pre-push gate — "
                      "remove the stale entry." % (k, section_name))
                fail = 1

    for g in letters:
        homes = [name for name, sec in
                 (("proofs", proofs), ("covered", covered), ("cannot_red", cannot)) if g in sec]

        if not homes:
            print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s runs in pre-push but is classified in neither "
                  "proofs, covered, nor cannot_red of gate-red-proofs.json — add a red-first test "
                  "that drives its check to a non-zero exit and register it as a proof, or declare "
                  "it covered with the reason it rides another gate." % g)
            fail = 1
            continue
        if len(homes) > 1:
            print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s is classified in more than one section (%s) — a "
                  "gate has one home in the registry." % (g, ", ".join(homes)))
            fail = 1
            continue

        home = homes[0]

        if home == "cannot_red":
            print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s is declared cannot_red (%s) — a gate that by "
                  "construction can never fail guards nothing. This is a finding, not a pass: give "
                  "the gate a red-first test, or the gate has no reason to run." % (g, cannot[g]))
            fail = 1
            continue

        if home == "covered":
            reason = covered[g]
            if not (isinstance(reason, str) and reason.strip()):
                print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s is declared covered but carries no reason — a "
                      "covered gate names the gate whose red it rides and why it holds no separate "
                      "fixture, so the line is settled rather than papered." % g)
                fail = 1
            continue

        # home == "proofs": verify the red proof by structure.
        entry = proofs[g]
        proof = entry.get("proof", "") if isinstance(entry, dict) else ""
        redtok = entry.get("reds", "") if isinstance(entry, dict) else ""

        if "::" not in proof:
            print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s proof %r is not in `<file>::<function>` form." % (g, proof))
            fail = 1
            continue
        relfile, fn = proof.split("::", 1)
        fpath = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, relfile)
        if not os.path.isfile(fpath):
            print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s proof file %s does not exist." % (g, relfile))
            fail = 1
            continue
        src = read(fpath)
        if not re.search(r"\bdef " + re.escape(fn) + r"\b", src):
            print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s proof function %s is not defined in %s." % (g, fn, relfile))
            fail = 1
            continue
        if not redtok or redtok not in src:
            print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s proof %s carries the reds token %r, which does not "
                  "appear in %s — the proof is not tied to this gate's check, so it cannot be shown "
                  "to drive the right gate to red." % (g, fn, redtok, relfile))
            fail = 1
            continue
        body = function_body(src, fn)
        if not body or not RED_ASSERT.search(body):
            print("every-gate-can-fail: gate %s proof %s in %s carries no non-zero-exit assertion — "
                  "a red proof must drive the check to red (assert its returncode is 1/2 or not 0), "
                  "not merely assert the gate ships." % (g, fn, relfile))
            fail = 1
            continue

    if fail == 0:
        print("every-gate-can-fail: OK (every pre-push gate carries a known-red proof or a declared "
              "covered ride; %d gates checked)." % len(letters))
    return fail


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""check-named-checks.py — gate ae: the check registry says what each runnable file is (SPEC INV-306).
3	
4	A skill body names a check by path. A project that adopts this pack holds almost none of those paths,
5	so the pack owes a record of what each named file is: what it does, which tree it judges, whether it
6	belongs in an adopting project, and what it needs to run. The record is `scripts/check-registry.json`.
7	This gate keeps that record true by recomputing every field from the tree.
8	
9	Eight arms:
10	
11	  A  key        — every key names an existing file under `scripts/` or `guardrails/`.
12	  B  kind       — check, library or data, recomputed from the tree and compared with the record.
13	  C  name       — a check carries a lowercase hyphenated handle, unique across the registry; a
14	                  library or a data entry carries none.
15	  D  reach      — every document name the entry's own code states appears in reach, read with
16	                  comments and docstrings stripped, where a reach member whose basename is that
17	                  name declares it; every reach member naming a path inside the pack exists in the
18	                  tree.
19	  E  needs      — every module the entry imports from `scripts/` or `guardrails/` appears in needs,
20	                  and every needs member is itself a registry key.
21	  F  root       — argument, working-directory or own-tree. One direction is proved: an entry
22	                  recorded argument or working-directory whose source carries a scan-root default
23	                  built from its own file's location reds. The reverse direction stays unproved, so
24	                  an entry recorded own-tree passes this arm on its record alone.
25	  G  domain     — a `scripts/` or `guardrails/` path standing in command position in a skill body
26	                  with no registry entry reds.
27	  H  kit        — kit is recomputed from reach and compared with the record, and a check whose kit
28	                  reads pack-only reds when a skill body names it in command position.
29	
30	Arms G and H read `skills/*/SKILL.md`. A skill's reference pages carry their own command lines and
31	join a later row.
32	
33	This gate judges the pack that holds it, so `--root` defaults to that pack's tree and the green line
34	names the tree it read. The checks the registry records are held to the host-root contract instead:
35	each of those takes the tree it judges as an argument.
36	
37	Usage:
38	  check-named-checks.py [--root DIR] [--registry PATH] [--skills DIR]
39	"""
40	import argparse
41	import io
42	import json
43	import os
44	import re
45	import sys
46	import tokenize
47	
48	CHECK = "check-named-checks"
49	HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
50	REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
51	
52	KINDS = ("check", "library", "data")
53	ROOTS = ("argument", "working-directory", "own-tree")
54	KITS = ("ships", "host-optional", "pack-only")
55	
56	# The directories holding machinery this pack authors. A reach member under one of them is what
57	# makes a check pack-only.
58	MACHINERY = ("guardrails", "scripts", "skills", "hooks", "adopt",
59	             "templates", "scaffold", "editions", "evals")
60	
61	NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$")
62	DOC_RE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z][A-Z_]{2,}\.md\b")
63	IMPORT_RE = re.compile(
64	    r"^\s*(?:from\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+import|import\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*))", re.M)
65	COMMAND_RE = re.compile(r"(?:python3\s+|bash\s+|sh\s+|\./)((?:scripts|guardrails)/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)")
66	MAIN_RE = re.compile(r"^if\s+__name__\s*==", re.M)
67	# A scan-root default that resolves to the directory holding the check's own file.
68	OWN_TREE_RE = re.compile(r"(?:default\s*=|DEFAULT_[A-Z_]*\s*=)[^\n#]*?"
69	                         r"(__file__|HERE|SCRIPT_DIR|REPO_ROOT)")
70	
71	
72	def read(path):
73	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
74	        return f.read()
75	
76	
77	def strip_python(src):
78	    """Return the source with comments and docstrings removed, so a name inside usage text passes."""
79	    out = []
80	    try:
81	        toks = list(tokenize.generate_tokens(io.StringIO(src).readline))
82	    except (tokenize.TokenError, IndentationError, SyntaxError):
83	        return src
84	    start_of_line = True
85	    for i, tok in enumerate(toks):
86	        if tok.type == tokenize.COMMENT:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check-named-checks.py — gate ae: the check registry says what each runnable file is (SPEC INV-306).

A skill body names a check by path. A project that adopts this pack holds almost none of those paths,
so the pack owes a record of what each named file is: what it does, which tree it judges, whether it
belongs in an adopting project, and what it needs to run. The record is `scripts/check-registry.json`.
This gate keeps that record true by recomputing every field from the tree.

Eight arms:

  A  key        — every key names an existing file under `scripts/` or `guardrails/`.
  B  kind       — check, library or data, recomputed from the tree and compared with the record.
  C  name       — a check carries a lowercase hyphenated handle, unique across the registry; a
                  library or a data entry carries none.
  D  reach      — every document name the entry's own code states appears in reach, read with
                  comments and docstrings stripped, where a reach member whose basename is that
                  name declares it; every reach member naming a path inside the pack exists in the
                  tree.
  E  needs      — every module the entry imports from `scripts/` or `guardrails/` appears in needs,
                  and every needs member is itself a registry key.
  F  root       — argument, working-directory or own-tree. One direction is proved: an entry
                  recorded argument or working-directory whose source carries a scan-root default
                  built from its own file's location reds. The reverse direction stays unproved, so
                  an entry recorded own-tree passes this arm on its record alone.
  G  domain     — a `scripts/` or `guardrails/` path standing in command position in a skill body
                  with no registry entry reds.
  H  kit        — kit is recomputed from reach and compared with the record, and a check whose kit
                  reads pack-only reds when a skill body names it in command position.

Arms G and H read `skills/*/SKILL.md`. A skill's reference pages carry their own command lines and
join a later row.

This gate judges the pack that holds it, so `--root` defaults to that pack's tree and the green line
names the tree it read. The checks the registry records are held to the host-root contract instead:
each of those takes the tree it judges as an argument.

Usage:
  check-named-checks.py [--root DIR] [--registry PATH] [--skills DIR]
"""
import argparse
import io
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tokenize

CHECK = "check-named-checks"
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)

KINDS = ("check", "library", "data")
ROOTS = ("argument", "working-directory", "own-tree")
KITS = ("ships", "host-optional", "pack-only")

# The directories holding machinery this pack authors. A reach member under one of them is what
# makes a check pack-only.
MACHINERY = ("guardrails", "scripts", "skills", "hooks", "adopt",
             "templates", "scaffold", "editions", "evals")

NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$")
DOC_RE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z][A-Z_]{2,}\.md\b")
IMPORT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:from\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+import|import\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*))", re.M)
COMMAND_RE = re.compile(r"(?:python3\s+|bash\s+|sh\s+|\./)((?:scripts|guardrails)/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)")
MAIN_RE = re.compile(r"^if\s+__name__\s*==", re.M)
# A scan-root default that resolves to the directory holding the check's own file.
OWN_TREE_RE = re.compile(r"(?:default\s*=|DEFAULT_[A-Z_]*\s*=)[^\n#]*?"
                         r"(__file__|HERE|SCRIPT_DIR|REPO_ROOT)")


def read(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return f.read()


def strip_python(src):
    """Return the source with comments and docstrings removed, so a name inside usage text passes."""
    out = []
    try:
        toks = list(tokenize.generate_tokens(io.StringIO(src).readline))
    except (tokenize.TokenError, IndentationError, SyntaxError):
        return src
    start_of_line = True
    for i, tok in enumerate(toks):
        if tok.type == tokenize.COMMENT:
            continue
        if tok.type == tokenize.STRING and start_of_line:
            j = i + 1
            while j < len(toks) and toks[j].type in (tokenize.COMMENT, tokenize.NL):
                j += 1
            if j < len(toks) and toks[j].type == tokenize.NEWLINE:
                continue
        if tok.type in (tokenize.NEWLINE, tokenize.NL, tokenize.INDENT,
                        tokenize.DEDENT, tokenize.ENCODING):
            if tok.type in (tokenize.NEWLINE, tokenize.NL):
                start_of_line = True
            out.append(tok.string)
            continue
        start_of_line = False
        out.append(tok.string + " ")
    return "".join(out)


def strip_shell(src):
    return "\n".join(re.sub(r"(^|\s)#.*$", r"\1", line) for line in src.splitlines())


def stripped_source(path, src):
    if path.endswith(".py"):
        return strip_python(src)
    if path.endswith(".sh"):
        return strip_shell(src)
    return src


def imported_modules(root, key, src):
    """Return the registry-shaped paths of the modules KEY imports from scripts/ or guardrails/."""
    found = set()
    for match in IMPORT_RE.finditer(src):
        name = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
        for directory in ("guardrails", "scripts"):
            candidate = "%s/%s.py" % (directory, name)
            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, candidate)) and candidate != key:
                found.add(candidate)
    return found


def has_entry_point(src):
    return src.startswith("#!") or bool(MAIN_RE.search(src))


def derive_kind(key, src, imported_by, referenced):
    """Return the kind the tree states for KEY, or None when no kind derives."""
    if key.endswith(".json"):
        return "data" if key in referenced else None
    if key in imported_by and not MAIN_RE.search(src or ""):
        return "library"
    if has_entry_point(src or ""):
        return "check"
    return None


def derive_kit(reach):
    if not reach:
        return "ships"
    for member in reach:
        head = member.split("/")[0]
        if "/" in member and head in MACHINERY:
            return "pack-only"
    return "host-optional"


def is_pack_path(root, member):
    """A reach member names a path inside the pack when its first segment is a pack directory."""
    if "/" not in member or member.startswith("~") or member.startswith("/"):
        return False
    head = member.split("/")[0]
    return os.path.isdir(os.path.join(root, head))


def own_tree_lines(src):
    return [i + 1 for i, line in enumerate(src.splitlines()) if OWN_TREE_RE.search(line)]


def command_positions(skills_dir):
    """Return (skill_body_count, [(relative path, line number, named path)])."""
    hits = []
    bodies = 0
    if not os.path.isdir(skills_dir):
        return 0, hits
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(skills_dir)):
        body = os.path.join(skills_dir, entry, "SKILL.md")
        if not os.path.isfile(body):
            continue
        bodies += 1
        for number, line in enumerate(read(body).splitlines(), 1):
            for match in COMMAND_RE.finditer(line):
                hits.append((body, number, match.group(1).rstrip(".,;:`)")))
    return bodies, hits


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="the check registry says what each runnable file is")
    parser.add_argument("--root", default=REPO_ROOT)
    parser.add_argument("--registry")
    parser.add_argument("--skills")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    root = os.path.abspath(args.root)
    registry_path = args.registry or os.path.join(root, "scripts", "check-registry.json")
    skills_dir = args.skills or os.path.join(root, "skills")
    registry_label = os.path.relpath(registry_path, root) if registry_path.startswith(root) \
        else registry_path

    findings = []

    if not os.path.exists(registry_path):
        print("%s: RED — the registry is missing at %s." % (CHECK, registry_path))
        print("  Fix: write the registry, one entry per runnable file a skill body names.")
        return 1

    try:
        data = json.loads(read(registry_path))
    except ValueError as err:
        print("%s: RED — the registry at %s does not parse: %s" % (CHECK, registry_label, err))
        print("  Fix: repair the JSON.")
        return 1

    entries = data.get("entries") or {}
    if not entries:
        print("%s: RED — the registry at %s holds 0 entries, so this run measured nothing."
              % (CHECK, registry_label))
        print("  Fix: fill the registry from the tree before running this gate.")
        return 1

    # ---- the tree, read once -------------------------------------------------------------
    sources = {}
    for key in entries:
        path = os.path.join(root, key)
        if os.path.isfile(path) and not key.endswith(".json"):
            try:
                sources[key] = read(path)
            except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                sources[key] = ""

    imported_by = set()
    for key, src in sources.items():
        imported_by |= imported_modules(root, key, src)

    referenced = set()
    for entry in entries.values():
        for member in list(entry.get("needs") or []) + list(entry.get("reach") or []):
            referenced.add(member)

    # ---- arm A: the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for key in sorted(entries):
        head = key.split("/")[0]
        if head not in ("scripts", "guardrails"):
            findings.append(
                ("A", "entry %s lies outside scripts/ and guardrails/, which bound the registry's "
                      "domain. Fix: drop the entry, or move the file into one of those two "
                      "directories." % key))
        elif not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, key)):
            findings.append(
                ("A", "entry %s names no file in the tree. Fix: correct the key to the file's "
                      "current path, or drop the entry." % key))

    # ---- arm B: the kind -----------------------------------------------------------------
    for key in sorted(entries):
        recorded = entries[key].get("kind")
        if recorded not in KINDS:
            findings.append(
                ("B", "entry %s records the kind %r, and the three kinds are check, library and "
                      "data. Fix: record one of the three." % (key, recorded)))
            continue
        if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, key)):
            continue
        derived = derive_kind(key, sources.get(key), imported_by, referenced)
        if derived is None:
            findings.append(
                ("B", "entry %s records the kind %s, and the tree states no kind for it: it carries "
                      "no entry point, no other entry imports it, and no entry reads it as data. "
                      "Fix: drop the entry, or give the file the shape its kind states."
                      % (key, recorded)))
        elif derived != recorded:
            findings.append(
                ("B", "entry %s records the kind %s, and the tree states %s. Fix: record the kind "
                      "the tree states." % (key, recorded, derived)))

    # ---- arm C: the name -----------------------------------------------------------------
    seen_names = {}
    for key in sorted(entries):
        entry = entries[key]
        name = entry.get("name")
        if entry.get("kind") == "check":
            if not name:
                findings.append(
                    ("C", "entry %s carries no name, and a check carries the handle a skill body "
                          "uses. Fix: add the name." % key))
                continue
            if not NAME_RE.match(name):
                findings.append(
                    ("C", "entry %s carries the name %r, and a name is lowercase words joined by "
                          "single hyphens. Fix: rewrite the name in that shape." % (key, name)))
            if name in seen_names:
                findings.append(
                    ("C", "entry %s carries the name %r, which entry %s already carries. Fix: give "
                          "one of the two a name of its own." % (key, name, seen_names[name])))
            else:
                seen_names[name] = key
        elif name:
            findings.append(
                ("C", "entry %s is a %s and carries the name %r, and nothing addresses a module or "
                      "a word list by name. Fix: drop the name."
                      % (key, entry.get("kind"), name)))

    # ---- arm D: the reach ----------------------------------------------------------------
    for key in sorted(entries):
        entry = entries[key]
        if entry.get("kind") != "check":
            if entry.get("reach"):
                findings.append(
                    ("D", "entry %s is a %s and carries a reach, and a reach belongs to a check. "
                          "Fix: drop the reach." % (key, entry.get("kind"))))
            continue
        reach = entry.get("reach")
        if reach is None:
            findings.append(
                ("D", "entry %s carries no reach, and a check states what it reads that nobody "
                      "handed it. Fix: add the reach, with an empty list where every target "
                      "arrives on the command line." % key))
            continue
        src = sources.get(key)
        if src is not None:
            declared = set(reach) | set(os.path.basename(m) for m in reach)
            for document in sorted(set(DOC_RE.findall(stripped_source(key, src)))):
                if document not in declared:
                    findings.append(
                        ("D", "entry %s states the document %s in its own code, and its reach does "
                              "not declare it. Fix: add %s to the reach, or take that document on "
                              "the command line." % (key, document, document)))
        for member in reach:
            if is_pack_path(root, member) and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, member)):
                findings.append(
                    ("D", "entry %s reaches %s, which the tree does not hold. Fix: correct the "
                          "reach member to the path it means, or drop it." % (key, member)))

    # ---- arm E: the needs ----------------------------------------------------------------
    for key in sorted(entries):
        entry = entries[key]
        kind = entry.get("kind")
        needs = entry.get("needs")
        if kind == "data":
            if needs:
                findings.append(
                    ("E", "entry %s is a data file and carries needs, and a data file reads "
                          "nothing. Fix: drop the needs." % key))
            continue
        if needs is None:
            findings.append(
                ("E", "entry %s carries no needs, and an entry states what it reads at run time. "
                      "Fix: add the needs, with an empty list where it reads nothing." % key))
            continue
        for member in needs:
            if member not in entries:
                findings.append(
                    ("E", "entry %s needs %s, which is no registry entry. Fix: give %s its own "
                          "entry, or drop it from the needs." % (key, member, member)))
        src = sources.get(key)
        if src:
            for module in sorted(imported_modules(root, key, src)):
                if module not in needs:
                    findings.append(
                        ("E", "entry %s imports the module %s, and its needs do not name it. Fix: "
                              "add %s to the needs." % (key, module, module)))

    # ---- arm F: the root -----------------------------------------------------------------
    for key in sorted(entries):
        entry = entries[key]
        if entry.get("kind") != "check":
            if entry.get("root"):
                findings.append(
                    ("F", "entry %s is a %s and records a root, and a root belongs to a check. "
                          "Fix: drop the root." % (key, entry.get("kind"))))
            continue
        recorded = entry.get("root")
        if recorded not in ROOTS:
            findings.append(
                ("F", "entry %s records the root %r, and the three roots are argument, "
                      "working-directory and own-tree. Fix: record one of the three."
                      % (key, recorded)))
            continue
        if recorded == "own-tree":
            continue
        src = sources.get(key)
        if not src:
            continue
        for line in own_tree_lines(src):
            findings.append(
                ("F", "entry %s records the root %s, and %s:%d sets a scan-root default built from "
                      "its own file's location. Fix: record the root own-tree, or take the tree on "
                      "the command line." % (key, recorded, key, line)))

    # ---- arms G and H: the registry against the skill bodies -----------------------------
    bodies, hits = command_positions(skills_dir)
    for body, number, named in hits:
        label = os.path.relpath(body, root) if body.startswith(root) else body
        entry = entries.get(named)
        if entry is None:
            findings.append(
                ("G", "%s:%d names %s in command position, and the registry holds no entry for it. "
                      "Fix: add the entry, or name the file in prose." % (label, number, named)))
            continue
        if entry.get("kind") == "check" and entry.get("kit") == "pack-only":
            reach = ", ".join(entry.get("reach") or []) or "this pack's own tree"
            findings.append(
                ("H", "%s:%d names the check %s in command position, and its kit reads pack-only "
                      "from the reach %s. Fix: name the check in prose, or move what it reads out "
                      "of the pack's own machinery." % (label, number, named, reach)))

    for key in sorted(entries):
        entry = entries[key]
        if entry.get("kind") != "check":
            if entry.get("kit"):
                findings.append(
                    ("H", "entry %s is a %s and records a kit, and a kit belongs to a check. Fix: "
                          "drop the kit." % (key, entry.get("kind"))))
            continue
        recorded = entry.get("kit")
        if recorded not in KITS:
            findings.append(
                ("H", "entry %s records the kit %r, and the three kits are ships, host-optional "
                      "and pack-only. Fix: record one of the three." % (key, recorded)))
            continue
        derived = derive_kit(entry.get("reach") or [])
        if derived != recorded:
            findings.append(
                ("H", "entry %s records the kit %s, and its reach derives %s. Fix: record the kit "
                      "its reach derives." % (key, recorded, derived)))

    # ---- the verdict ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    if findings:
        print("%s: RED — %d finding(s) over %d registry entries and %d skill bodies."
              % (CHECK, len(findings), len(entries), bodies))
        for arm, message in findings:
            print("  arm %s: %s" % (arm, message))
        print('{"severity":"error","code":"%s","findings":%d}' % (CHECK, len(findings)))
        return 1

    kinds = {}
    for entry in entries.values():
        kinds[entry.get("kind")] = kinds.get(entry.get("kind"), 0) + 1
    print("%s: OK — reach: registry=%s; %d entries read (%d checks, %d libraries, %d data files); "
          "%d skill bodies scanned; %d command-position paths found; tree=%s"
          % (CHECK, registry_label, len(entries), kinds.get("check", 0), kinds.get("library", 0),
             kinds.get("data", 0), bodies, len(hits), root))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# check-ci-mirror.sh — the CI mirror carries every local gate (SPEC INV-210, gate u).
     3	#
     4	# The push gate lives twice: guardrails/pre-push runs it on this machine, and
     5	# .github/workflows/gates.yml re-runs it in CI as the second, any-machine net (SPEC M-5).
     6	# gates.yml is hand-maintained, so it drifts the moment a gate is added locally and the CI
     7	# file is not touched — the worked instance: gates h, k, and n were missing from CI on
     8	# 2026-07-18, so a push a green CI would wave through could still fail the local gate.
     9	#
    10	# This check reads the gate letters pre-push invokes (the "-- gate X:" markers) and the gate
    11	# letters gates.yml invokes (the "gate X" tokens in its step names), subtracts the declared CI
    12	# carve-outs (guardrails/ci-mirror.json — the gates a CI checkout legitimately cannot or need
    13	# not re-run, each with its reason), and reds on any local gate letter missing from CI, naming
    14	# the gate and the one fix. It is the kin of config-health (gate m): that proves the installed
    15	# hook matches its source, this proves the CI mirror matches the source too.
    16	
    17	set -euo pipefail
    18	
    19	# Resolve the repo root from the script's own location, not git, so the check runs the same in
    20	# a scratch copy the suite makes (the scratch tree drops .git by design) as on the real tree.
    21	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    22	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
    23	PREPUSH="${CI_MIRROR_PREPUSH:-$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/pre-push}"
    24	GATES_YML="${CI_MIRROR_GATES_YML:-$REPO_ROOT/.github/workflows/gates.yml}"
    25	CARVE_JSON="${CI_MIRROR_JSON:-$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/ci-mirror.json}"
    26	
    27	for f in "$PREPUSH" "$GATES_YML" "$CARVE_JSON"; do
    28	  if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
    29	    echo "ci-mirror: cannot read $f — the gate stands on all three files."
    30	    exit 1
    31	  fi
    32	done
    33	
    34	fail=0
    35	
    36	# Local gate letters: the "-- gate X:" markers pre-push echoes before each gate.
    37	local_letters="$(grep -oE -- '-- gate [a-z]{1,2}:' "$PREPUSH" | grep -oE '[a-z]{1,2}:' | tr -d ':' | sort -u || true)"
    38	
    39	# CI gate letters: the "gate X" tokens inside gates.yml step names (a "name:" line).
    40	ci_letters="$(grep -E 'name:.*gate [a-z]' "$GATES_YML" | grep -oE 'gate [a-z]{1,2}' | grep -oE '[a-z]{1,2}$' | sort -u || true)"
    41	
    42	# Declared carve-outs: gates a CI checkout does not re-run, each with its reason.
    43	carve="$(jq -r '.ci_excluded | keys[]' "$CARVE_JSON" | sort -u || true)"
    44	
    45	in_set() {  # in_set <letter> <newline-separated set>
    46	  printf '%s\n' $2 | grep -qx "$1"
    47	}
    48	
    49	# A carve-out must name a real local gate — a stale carve-out is itself drift.
    50	for c in $carve; do
    51	  if ! in_set "$c" "$local_letters"; then
    52	    echo "ci-mirror: carve-out '$c' in ci-mirror.json names no local pre-push gate — remove the stale carve-out."
    53	    fail=1
    54	  fi
    55	done
    56	
    57	# Every local gate letter must be mirrored in CI, or declared a carve-out with its reason.
    58	for g in $local_letters; do
    59	  if in_set "$g" "$ci_letters"; then
    60	    continue
    61	  fi
    62	  if in_set "$g" "$carve"; then
    63	    continue
    64	  fi
    65	  echo "ci-mirror: gate $g runs in guardrails/pre-push but is absent from .github/workflows/gates.yml — add its step to gates.yml, or declare it in guardrails/ci-mirror.json with the reason it stays out of CI."
    66	  fail=1
    67	done
    68	
    69	if [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; then
    70	  echo "ci-mirror: OK (every local pre-push gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out)."
    71	fi
    72	exit "$fail"
